reason: E2 directly demonstrates that phase inversion from a continuous B2 matrix to a continuous BCC matrix with discrete B2 precipitates substantially increases compressive ductility in a related alloy, supporting the core mechanism. However, E1 shows brittleness under tension in a different alloy after HIP, and neither cited study provides evidence on HfZrTiTa0.53 specifically, on tensile ductility improvement via this mechanism, or on impact energy release, leaving several premises unsupported.
premises: A continuous ordered B2 phase causes brittleness in refractory alloys.
Phase inversion (disordered BCC matrix + discrete B2 precipitates) improves ductility.
The proposed heat treatment can achieve this phase inversion in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Improved tensile ductility can be achieved while maintaining high strength.
Impact-triggered energy release will be maintained after microstructural change.
